summary.intent: Execute phase 19.1 (Extract Core Crypto SDK as Shared Package) using GSD wave-based parallel execution, starting with Wave 1 plans to split the crypto package and expand the API client.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 was initiated with 2 parallel subagents spawned for plans 19.1-01 and 19.1-02; execution was interrupted before completion. An earlier attempt on phase 9.1 was also interrupted.

repo: Phase 19.1 has 6 plans across 5 waves, targeting extraction of a shared crypto SDK
Planning docs for phase 19.1 live on the `docs/phase-19.1-context` branch, requiring the execution branch to be created from there
The project uses pnpm workspaces with packages like @cipherbox/crypto, @cipherbox/core, and @cipherbox/api-client
The api-client package was previously a bare openapi.json file without a full typed HTTP client
workflow: GSD execute-phase initializes via `gsd-tools init execute-phase` which returns phase_found, plans, waves, and executor_model config in one call
The stale auto-chain flag must be cleared before reading config when --auto is not passed to prevent unintended auto-advance
Subagents are spawned with subagent_type=gsd-executor and pass only file paths — executors read files themselves to keep orchestrator context lean (~10-15%)
Wave grouping is retrieved via `gsd-tools phase-plan-index` which returns each plan's wave assignment, autonomy flag, and task count

friction: First invocation targeted wrong phase (9.1 instead of 19.1) and was manually interrupted by the user
Branch management complexity: planning docs were on a non-main branch, requiring the execution branch to be derived from it rather than main
